finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated `host` query parameter is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, so shell metacharacters (; | $() backticks, &&) execute arbitrary commands as the server user. Output is returned in the response, so the result is directly visible to the attacker.
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which spawns /bin/sh -c

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated directly into the shell command string passed to exec()
Command stdout returned in response (res.send(out)), giving the attacker output of injected commands

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or escaping on host. No authentication or authorization middleware on the app. No use of execFile or an argv array. Also, req.query.host can be an array or object (Express qs parser), but that does not block exploitation. A value starting with '-' would also allow ping option injection. The /version route uses execFile with fixed args (safe), and /uptime uses exec with a constant string (safe, no user input).

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host straight to exec (shell) in the unauthenticated GET /ping handler (tools.js:6), with no validation or auth middleware, and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so `;`-style injection (exit status of the last command) yields visible command output.

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec (which runs /bin/sh -c) with no auth, validation or escaping anywhere in the file, and tools.js:11 returns stdout; `host=x; id` exits 0 via the last command, so the output is returned.
